footer.aboutTitle: About This Train Driver Entrance Exam
footer.topicText: This fictional aptitude challenge uses display-board reading, timing, route logic, observation, sequencing, and prioritization to create a fun staged test.
footer.aboutText: This fictional aptitude challenge explores display-board reading, timing, route logic, observation, sequencing, and calm prioritization. It is for entertainment and self-challenge only—not an official railway recruitment test, licensing assessment, training program, operating manual, or professional qualification. Every rule needed to answer is stated inside the question.

stageGroups.title: Platform Scan
stageGroups.encouragement: Eyes sharp. The departure board is about to get busier.

questions.prompt: Four departures flash up: Lakeside P2, Hilltown P3, Lakeside P5, Rivergate P1. Which platform serves Hilltown?
questions.explanation: Hilltown appears once, beside Platform 3.

questions.prompt: Your cab checklist is key, radio, flashlight, route card. You have the key, flashlight, and route card. What is missing?
questions.explanation: The radio is the only checklist item not accounted for.

questions.prompt: You face north. The control room is east and the staff exit is west. What is on your right?
questions.explanation: East is to your right when facing north.

questions.prompt: The display changes from NORTHBAY · 14:10 · P6 to NORTHBAY · 14:40 · P6. What changed?
questions.explanation: The destination and platform stay the same; only the time changes.

questions.prompt: A quick scan shows: amber, white, blue, amber, red. Which color appears twice?
questions.explanation: Amber appears first and fourth.

questions.prompt: Along the concourse the order is Gate A, elevator, café, Gate B. What sits directly between Gate A and the café?
questions.explanation: The elevator is immediately after Gate A and before the café.

questions.prompt: A notice reads: ‘Platform 1 opens at 09:00.’ The clock shows 08:57. What is the correct reading?
questions.explanation: From 08:57 to 09:00 is three minutes.

stageGroups.title: Departure Board
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice work. Now beat the clock without rushing the math.

questions.prompt: Compare: COASTLINE · 11:20 · P5 · ON TIME and COASTLINE · 11:35 · P5 · ON TIME. Which field differs?
questions.explanation: Every field matches except 11:20 versus 11:35.

questions.prompt: Board A stops at Northbay, Elm Park, Rivergate. Board B stops at Northbay, Rivergate. Which stop has vanished?
questions.explanation: Elm Park appears only on Board A.

questions.prompt: Legend: ◆ limited stop · ● all stops · ★ bicycle space. The 12:10 has ◆ and ★. What can you conclude?
questions.explanation: The service carries both the limited-stop diamond and bicycle-space star.

questions.prompt: The route sequence is Pine → Lake → Market → Harbour. Which option preserves the middle two stops?
questions.explanation: Only the first option keeps Lake then Market in their original positions.

questions.prompt: The 16:05 to Oakfield moves 10 minutes later and switches from P4 to P6. Which updated line is correct?
questions.explanation: Ten minutes after 16:05 is 16:15, and the new platform is 6.

questions.prompt: Board key: Q = quiet car, B = bicycle space. A service shows Q but not B. What does it offer?
questions.explanation: Q is present and B is absent, so only the quiet car is shown.

questions.prompt: The board cycles 07 PINE, 09 LAKE, 12 MARKET, 14 COAST. Which entry comes immediately after 09 LAKE?
questions.explanation: 12 MARKET directly follows 09 LAKE in the displayed order.

stageGroups.title: Beat the Clock
stageGroups.encouragement: Right on time. Next you take control of the route map.

questions.prompt: A train leaves at 09:15 and arrives at 09:50. How long is the journey?
questions.explanation: From 09:15 to 09:50 is 35 minutes.

questions.prompt: A service due at 12:40 is delayed by 15 minutes. When is it now due?
questions.explanation: 12:40 plus 15 minutes is 12:55.

questions.prompt: It is 17:20. Briefing takes 8 minutes and the train leaves at 17:45. How much spare time remains after briefing?
questions.explanation: There are 25 minutes to departure; after an 8-minute briefing, 17 minutes remain.

questions.prompt: Train A leaves at 08:50 and takes 45 minutes. Train B leaves at 09:05 and takes 25 minutes. Which arrives first?
questions.explanation: A arrives at 09:35; B arrives at 09:30, five minutes earlier.

questions.prompt: A journey takes 40 minutes. It starts at 13:25. When does it finish?
questions.explanation: 13:25 plus 40 minutes is 14:05.

questions.prompt: Services depart at 10:30, 10:50 and 11:10. If the pattern continues, when is the next one?
questions.explanation: The pattern advances by 20 minutes, making the next time 11:30.

questions.prompt: A 14:00 departure moves 20 minutes earlier, then gains a 5-minute delay. What is the final time?
questions.explanation: Moving earlier gives 13:40; adding five minutes gives 13:45.

stageGroups.title: Route Control
stageGroups.encouragement: Route set. The signals now introduce a new rulebook.

questions.prompt: From the station, move two squares north and one east. Where are you relative to the start?
questions.explanation: The final position is both north and east of the starting point.

questions.prompt: Route A has 3 stops and avoids Platform 4. Route B has 5 stops and passes through blocked Platform 4. Which route both has fewer stops and avoids the blocked platform?
questions.explanation: Route A has fewer stops and is explicitly stated to avoid blocked Platform 4.

questions.prompt: A route instruction says: go east, then north. Where are you relative to the start?
questions.explanation: East followed by north ends north-east of the start.

questions.prompt: The depot is north of Central. Harbour is east of the depot. Where is Harbour from Central?
questions.explanation: North followed by east places Harbour north-east of Central.

questions.prompt: Platforms 1, 2, and 3 are open; Platform 4 is blocked. Route X uses Platforms 2 then 3, while Route Y uses Platform 4. Which route is available?
questions.explanation: Route X uses only open Platforms 2 and 3; Route Y uses blocked Platform 4.

questions.prompt: Route A is 12 minutes with one change. Route B is 15 minutes direct. You must avoid changes. Which route fits?
questions.explanation: Route B is the only direct route, even though it takes three minutes longer.

questions.prompt: Route: Start → Bridge → Tunnel → Junction → End. Which two locations sit between Bridge and End?
questions.explanation: Tunnel and Junction are the two stops after Bridge and before End.

stageGroups.title: Signal Logic
stageGroups.encouragement: Signals understood. Now execute every check in the right order.

questions.prompt: Amber means wait; white means confirmed. A route has a white card and an amber marker. Markers take priority. What happens first?
questions.explanation: The amber instruction comes first, so the team waits even though the route has a white confirmation card.

questions.prompt: A double bell means check the display board first. The board says Platform 2, while the route card says Platform 5. Which action follows the bell rule?
questions.explanation: The double-bell rule requires the display board to be checked before either platform is chosen.

questions.prompt: Fictional rules: Signal A means continue to the listed route; Signal B means wait for confirmation. Signal B appears while a shorter route is offered. What should happen?
questions.explanation: Signal B requires waiting for confirmation, regardless of the shorter route.

questions.prompt: White means confirmed; amber means hold. Route A is white but longer. Route B is amber but shorter. Which can be selected now?
questions.explanation: Only Route A is confirmed; the shorter Route B remains on hold.

questions.prompt: If the display and route card disagree, verify the display before choosing. The display says P2; the card says P3. What happens first?
questions.explanation: The stated rule requires checking the display before choosing between the two platforms.

questions.prompt: Green means open; amber means wait. Route C is green with 4 stops; Route D is amber with 2. Open routes come first. Which fits?
questions.explanation: Route C is marked open; Route D requires waiting despite having fewer stops.

questions.prompt: A red marker means read the attached note before choosing. The note changes the platform from 3 to 6. Which action must occur before Platform 6 can be chosen?
questions.explanation: The red-marker rule requires the note to be read before its Platform 6 update is used.

stageGroups.title: Sequence Control
stageGroups.encouragement: Clean sequence. Next comes a rapid-fire detail check.

questions.prompt: Checklist: read the board, check the route card, then choose a platform. The board and route card have both been checked and now agree on Platform 3. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The first two checks are complete, so the final checklist step is choosing the agreed Platform 3.

questions.prompt: Rule: verify the time before comparing platforms. The time has been verified as 13:20, but Platforms 2 and 5 have not been compared. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Time verification is complete, so platform comparison is the next stated step.

questions.prompt: Three checks must satisfy both rules: the board before the route card, and the route card before the marker. Which order works?
questions.explanation: Board, card, marker is the only order that satisfies both stated dependencies.

questions.prompt: Rule: check uncertain details before acting. The time is confirmed, but the platform number is uncertain. Which step must occur before the route is chosen?
questions.explanation: The platform is the only uncertain detail, so it must be checked before choosing the route.

questions.prompt: A board update must be read after the bell and before the route card. Which sequence is correct?
questions.explanation: The board sits between the bell and route card.

questions.prompt: Protocol: confirm marker → confirm time → choose route → announce. The marker and time are confirmed. What comes next?
questions.explanation: With the first two checks complete, choosing the route is next.

questions.prompt: The update must be checked before the schedule is shared, and the schedule must be shared before boarding. Which action is last?
questions.explanation: The required order ends with boarding after the checked schedule is shared.

stageGroups.title: Detail Detective
stageGroups.encouragement: Nothing slipped past you. Now decide what matters first.

questions.prompt: Quick recall: on the earlier board key, which letter marked a quiet car?
questions.explanation: The departure-board key defined Q as quiet car.

questions.prompt: Card A says Platform 2, 10:20. Card B says Platform 2, 10:50. What is different?
questions.explanation: Both cards name Platform 2, but their times differ.

questions.prompt: Board A lists Oak, Pine, Lake, Hill. Board B lists Oak, Pine, Hill. Which stop appears only on Board A?
questions.explanation: Lake is the only stop present on Board A and absent from Board B.

questions.prompt: Card A says Gate C, 16:20, Northbay. Card B says Gate D, 16:20, Northbay. Which detail differs?
questions.explanation: The time and destination match; only the gate changes from C to D.

questions.prompt: Notice A says Riverline, 18:10, Platform 1. Notice B says Coastline, 18:10, Platform 6. Which detail matches?
questions.explanation: Both notices show 18:10, while their routes and platforms differ.

questions.prompt: Board: Oak, Pine, Elm, Coast. Card: Oak, Elm, Pine, Coast. What changed?
questions.explanation: Oak and Coast stay fixed; only Pine and Elm exchange positions.

questions.prompt: The board reads Circle 7, Square 9, Triangle 4. The route card reads Circle 7, Square 6, Triangle 4. Which symbol has the mismatched number?
questions.explanation: Square is paired with 9 on the board and 6 on the route card; the other pairs match.

stageGroups.title: Control Room
stageGroups.encouragement: Good judgement. Now the same decisions arrive under pressure.

questions.prompt: Rule: safety confirmation comes before speed. One route is faster, but its platform detail is unconfirmed. What has priority?
questions.explanation: The stated rule puts confirmation before speed.

questions.prompt: Earlier, Platform 4 was delayed. Before directing a passenger group there, what should you check first?
questions.explanation: The known delay makes the current platform status the relevant first check.

questions.prompt: Conflicting updates must be checked before sharing. A says 14:10; B says 14:40 but its source is unreadable. What comes first?
questions.explanation: Update B contains the uncertain source detail, so that source must be verified before either time is shared.

questions.prompt: The confirmed board says P2. A smudged note might say P7. Rule: confirmed information leads until unclear information is checked. What guides the next choice?
questions.explanation: The board is confirmed; the note is not yet reliable.

questions.prompt: Rule: if a route is blocked, do not select it even if it is shorter. Route A is blocked and Route B is open. Which route can be selected?
questions.explanation: Only the open route meets the rule.

questions.prompt: Check missing details before finalizing. Route A has a confirmed time but no platform; Route B is complete. What must happen before Route A is finalized?
questions.explanation: Route A is missing its platform, so that detail must be checked before Route A can be finalized.

questions.prompt: Priority rule: confirmed information outranks preference. Route A is preferred but unconfirmed; Route B is confirmed and open. Which route has priority?
questions.explanation: Route B has priority because it is confirmed and open, while Route A is only preferred.

stageGroups.title: Under Pressure
stageGroups.encouragement: Calm and controlled. One final run remains.

questions.prompt: Two updates arrive: the display says 15:30, while the route card has no time. Rule: verify missing details before acting. What should you verify?
questions.explanation: The route card is missing the relevant time detail.

questions.prompt: The display says Platform 2 at 16:10; the route card says Platform 5 at 16:10. Rule: verify the display before choosing when platforms conflict. What is the next step?
questions.explanation: The times match but the platforms conflict, so the stated rule requires the display to be verified.

questions.prompt: Earlier, Signal B meant wait for confirmation. Signal B is showing and a new route looks shorter. What should happen first?
questions.explanation: The Signal B rule still applies before choosing a route.

questions.prompt: A route card says Platform 6; the board marks Platform 6 delayed. Rule: check a known delay before using that platform. Which detail should be checked?
questions.explanation: Platform 6 has the known delay, so its current status is the relevant detail to check.

questions.prompt: Thirty seconds remain. Route A is open with a confirmed time; Route B is open with an unconfirmed time. Confirmed details win. Which has the stronger basis?
questions.explanation: Time pressure does not make Route B's unconfirmed time more reliable.

questions.prompt: Route A has a confirmed time but no platform. Route B is complete but closed. Never guess or use a closed route. What should happen?
questions.explanation: Route B cannot be used because it is closed, while Route A becomes usable only after its missing platform is verified.

questions.prompt: The board shows P3 but its destination is unreadable. The card shows P3 and Northbay. Unclear board details must be verified. What comes first?
questions.explanation: The platform matches, but the board destination is unclear and must be verified under the stated rule.

questions.prompt: Final run: depart 10:20, travel 25 minutes, then allow a 5-minute platform hold. When are you clear?
questions.explanation: Travel ends at 10:45; the five-minute hold ends at 10:50.

questions.prompt: Blue means quiet. Route Blue has 3 stops and takes 28 minutes; Route Red has 5 stops and takes 25. Which is quiet with fewer stops?
questions.explanation: Blue satisfies the quiet requirement and has fewer stops, despite taking three minutes longer.

questions.prompt: Signal B says wait. Board and route card disagree, and the display must be verified before choosing. Which sequence follows both rules?
questions.explanation: Signal B requires waiting for confirmation; the conflict rule then requires display verification before a platform is chosen.

questions.prompt: P4 leaves at 11:10 but has an unknown delay. P2 leaves at 11:20 on time. You must arrive by 11:45 and either trip takes 20 minutes. What must be checked first?
questions.explanation: P4 could arrive by 11:45 only if its delay is no more than 15 minutes, so that uncertainty comes first.

questions.prompt: From Central go east, north, then west by equal distances. Where do you finish relative to Central?
questions.explanation: The east and west moves cancel, leaving you north of Central.

questions.prompt: Checklist: check the time, check the marker, then choose. The time is confirmed and the marker is blue, meaning quiet route. Which action completes the checklist?
questions.explanation: Both checks are complete, and the blue marker identifies the quiet route to choose.

questions.prompt: Blue marks the quiet route. Platform 4 is delayed. Signal B says wait. The board offers blue Platform 2 or delayed Platform 4. Which sequence uses every clue?
questions.explanation: Signal B requires waiting first. Platform 4's delay is then checked, and the blue marker identifies Platform 2 as the quiet choice.
